summary: This note is a broad overview of Indian history, from Neolithic settlement and the ancient Maurya, Shunga, Satavahana and Kushan empires through the Gupta Golden Age, the Delhi Sultanate and Mughal Empire, and the British East India Company's rise after Plassey. It also covers regional powers such as the Ahom Kingdom and the Medieval Cholas, and social and intellectual movements like the Bengal Renaissance and Young Bengal.
one_line: A broad survey of Indian history from Neolithic settlement and ancient empires through the Mughals, the British East India Company, and the Chola naval power.
key_facts: The Kabul Shahi dynasties ruled the Kabul Valley and Gandhara from the decline of the Kushan Empire in the 3rd century to the early 9th century.
The change-over from the Buddhist Shahis to the Hindu Shahis is thought to have occurred sometime around 870.
Classical India refers to the period when much of the Indian subcontinent was reunited under the Gupta Empire (c. 320–550 CE).
Early Hindu numerals had only nine symbols until 600 to 800 CE, when a symbol for zero was developed for the numeral system.
The first confirmed semipermanent settlements appeared 9,000 years ago in the Bhimbetka rock shelters in modern Madhya Pradesh, India.
The Shunga Empire controlled vast areas of the Indian subcontinent from around 187 to 78 BCE and was established by Pushyamitra Shunga after the fall of the Maurya Empire.
Pushyamitra Shunga ruled for 36 years and was succeeded by his son Agnimitra; there were ten Shunga rulers.
The Delhi Sultanate was founded in 1206 CE by the Central Asian Turks.
The Battle of Plassey took place on 23 June 1757, when the Bengal Army of the East India Company, led by Robert Clive, defeated the French-supported Nawab's forces.
After the Battle of Buxar in 1764, the East India Company acquired the rights of administration in Bengal from the de jure Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II.
In 1526 Babur, a Timurid descendant from the Fergana Valley, swept across the Khyber Pass and established the Mughal Empire.
Humayun was defeated by the Afghan warrior Sher Shah Suri in 1540 and was forced to retreat to Kabul.
Akbar's forces defeated and killed Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat on 6 November 1556.
The Satavahana Empire was based from Amaravati in Andhra Pradesh and covered much of India from 230 BCE onward; it was one of the first Indian states to issue coins struck with rulers embossed.
The Kushan Empire expanded under its first emperor, Kujula Kadphises, about the middle of the 1st century CE, and by the time of his grandson Kanishka had conquered most of northern India.

entities.name: Kabul Shahi dynasties
entities.role: Dynasties that ruled the Kabul Valley and Gandhara from the decline of the Kushan Empire to the early 9th century

entities.name: Kushan Empire
entities.role: Central Asian-origin empire that expanded into the northwest of the subcontinent under Kujula Kadphises

entities.name: Gupta Empire
entities.role: Empire that reunited much of the subcontinent (c. 320–550 CE) and marked the Golden Age of India

entities.name: Shunga Empire
entities.role: Ancient Indian dynasty from Magadha that controlled vast areas from around 187 to 78 BCE

entities.name: Pushyamitra Shunga
entities.role: Founder of the Shunga Empire who ruled for 36 years

entities.name: Agnimitra
entities.role: Son of Pushyamitra Shunga who succeeded him as ruler

entities.name: Bhagabhadra
entities.role: Later Shunga emperor who held court at Besnagar, modern Vidisha

entities.name: Maurya Empire
entities.role: Empire that conquered most of the subcontinent in the 4th and 3rd centuries BCE, before the Shunga Empire

entities.name: Bhimbetka rock shelters
entities.role: Site in modern Madhya Pradesh with the first confirmed semipermanent settlements, 9,000 years ago

entities.name: Delhi Sultanate
entities.role: Muslim state founded in 1206 CE by Central Asian Turks that ruled much of northern India in the early 14th century

entities.name: Mughal Empire
entities.role: Empire founded by Babur in 1526 that at its zenith covered Afghanistan, Pakistan, India and Bangladesh

entities.name: Babur
entities.role: Timurid descendant from the Fergana Valley who established the Mughal Empire in 1526

entities.name: Humayun
entities.role: Mughal ruler, son of Babur, defeated by Sher Shah Suri in 1540

entities.name: Sher Shah Suri
entities.role: Afghan warrior who defeated Humayun in 1540

entities.name: Hemu Vikramaditya
entities.role: Hindu emperor who established secular rule in North India from Delhi until 1556

entities.name: Akbar
entities.role: Mughal ruler whose forces defeated and killed Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat

entities.name: Second Battle of Panipat
entities.role: Battle on 6 November 1556 in which Akbar's forces defeated and killed Hemu

entities.name: Battle of Plassey
entities.role: Battle on 23 June 1757 in which the East India Company's Bengal Army defeated the French-supported Nawab's forces

entities.name: Robert Clive
entities.role: Commander of the East India Company's Bengal Army at Plassey and its first Governor of Bengal in 1757

entities.name: Siraj Ud Daulah
entities.role: Nawab of Bengal, de facto ruler of the Bengal province, who opposed British attempts to use these permits

entities.name: East India Company
entities.role: British company that extended control over Bengal and monopolized its trade

entities.name: Battle of Buxar
entities.role: 1764 battle after which the company acquired rights of administration in Bengal

entities.name: Shah Alam II
entities.role: De jure Mughal Emperor who granted the company the rights of administration in Bengal

entities.name: Satavahana Empire
entities.role: Royal Indian dynasty based at Amaravati, Junnar and Prathisthan that covered much of India from 230 BCE onward

entities.name: Kujula Kadphises
entities.role: First emperor of the Kushan Empire

entities.name: Kanishka
entities.role: Grandson of Kujula Kadphises under whom the Kushans conquered most of northern India

entities.name: Ahom Kingdom
entities.role: Kingdom and tribe that ruled much of Assam from the 13th century until British rule was established in 1838

entities.name: Emperor Harsha
entities.role: Emperor of Kannauj who reunited northern India in the 7th century after the collapse of the Gupta dynasty

entities.name: Medieval Cholas
entities.role: South Indian dynasty that rose to prominence in the mid-9th century and built the greatest empire South India had seen

entities.name: Rajaraja Chola I
entities.role: Chola ruler who gave political unity to Southern India and established the Chola Empire as a sea power

entities.name: Rajendra Chola I
entities.role: Chola ruler whose navies extended Chola influence to Southeast Asia and who led an expedition to the Ganges

entities.name: Young Bengal movement
entities.role: Early social movement that espoused rationalism and atheism among upper caste educated Hindus
